newsitem.title: USA: Nord sees Tritton decision in late 1997.
newsitem.headline: Nord sees Tritton decision in late 1997.

text.p: Nord Pacific Ltd said Friday a development decision on the Tritton Copper Project in New South Wales, Australia, can be expected in late 1997 with initial production possible in early 1999.
The company has a 50 percent interest in the project with the rest held by Straits Resources Ltd.

Nord said Tritton reserves are now estimated at 9.75 million metric tonnes grading 3.01 percent copper, 0.21 grams per tonn gold and 11 grams per tonne silver containing 646 million pounds of copper, 66,000 ounces of gold and 3.4 million ounces of silver.

In August, the company said Tritton was estimate4d -- measured, indicated and inferred -- to contain 238,000 tonnes of copper, 60,000 oumnces of gold and 3 million ounces of silver. At the time, it said this preliminary estimatre was based on data from 105 holes drilled to depths of up to 800 meters.

The latest estimate is based on 115 holes drilled to depts of up to 1,000 meters, Nord said, adding the deposit has not been closed at depth by drilling and further increases in resource estimates are likely.
"The new resource estimate indicates that Tritton is a very significant copper deposit, and also contains substantial amounts of both gold and silver," the company said.

"Feasibility work to date ... has included prelimnary estimates of capital and operating costs. Results ... suggest that Tritton could become a low cost producer of copper, with byproduct precious metals credits," it continued.
